title.narrative: Emergency assistance to 500 new households in the Congolese refugees camp of Kigeme (Rwanda)

description.narrative:
Following the clashes between the FARDC (DRC government army) and the armed group called "M23" in the province of North Kivu, Rwanda hosted on its territory more than 4,000 households of Congolese refugees since the month of May 2012. First, they were in camp of Nkamira in the diocese of Nyundo before being transferred to the camp of Kigeme which is in the diocese of Gikongoro. With aid from 8 Caritas members of the Network Caritas Internationalis, Caritas Rwanda was able to provide assistance to these families with non-food items, including blankets, jerry cans, plates, spoons, cups, ladles , soap, buckets, mats, napkins, toilet paper, pots, cloths for ladies and thrift stores for children and adults. All these aids were highly appreciated by the beneficiaries who arrived in Rwanda stripped of everything. Today, despite the assistance provided by the Caritas Rwanda, the Government and other humanitarian organizations, the need for food and non-food items remain enormous in Kigeme camp. In addition to 4000 refugee households already living in that camp, there have added other hundreds of people who fled the fighting that led to the fall of Goma; most of them are women and children. Note that women and children are the most affected of this war and require special attention. Caritas Rwanda continues its advocacy work for these people in need with humanitarian organizations to find one that could help relieve their misery.
Caritas Rwanda would like to assist 500 households from these newly arrived in order to reduce the vulnerability of women and children affected by the violence of armed conflict by facilitating their access to non-food items.
Trough this project, each targeted household will receive 8 pieces of clothing for children, 12 soaps for body care and laundry, 2 cotton flannels and 1 loincloth for women.
The project will be implemented by Caritas Rwanda staff with support from CAFOD emergency team and in close collaboration/coordination with other humanitarian actors involved in assistance at Kigeme camp.
